title: Merge Nodes in Between Zeros
description:
You are given the `head` of a singly linked list containing a series of integers separated by `0`s. Both the beginning and end of the linked list have `Node.val == 0`, and there are no two consecutive nodes with `Node.val == 0`.

For every two consecutive `0`s, merge all nodes strictly between them into a single node whose value is the sum of all the merged nodes. The modified list must not contain any `0`s.

Return the head of the modified linked list.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [3, 2 * 10^4].
There are no two consecutive nodes with Node.val == 0.
The first and last nodes both have Node.val == 0.
hints: Reuse existing nodes in-place by maintaining a `write` pointer for the output list and a `read` pointer scanning segments between zeros.

Whenever `read.val == 0`, store the accumulated segment sum into `write.val`, and if more segments remain (`read.next != null`), advance `write` to `write.next`; otherwise terminate with `write.next = null`.

examples.explanation: Between the first two zeros is [3, 1] summing to 4; between the next two is [4, 5, 2] summing to 11.
Segments [1], [3], and [2, 2] sum to 1, 3, and 4 respectively.
Only one segment [7] lies between the two bounding zeros, producing [7].
